key_insight: LeapAlign enables effective post‑training alignment of flow matching generative models by backpropagating reward signals through short, two‑step trajectories, avoiding the memory and gradient‑stability issues of full long‑trajectory backpropagation.
problem_solved: Directly fine‑tuning flow matching models by backpropagating reward gradients through long generation trajectories is memory‑intensive and prone to gradient explosion, which prevents effective updates to early generation steps that determine global structure.
method: Construct two‑step surrogate trajectories that bridge an arbitrary intermediate generation step to a later/final state, drastically shortening paths for gradient flow.
Backpropagate reward gradients through these short trajectories to update parameters at any generation step (including early steps) with reduced memory and stabilised gradients.
Apply this procedure as a post‑training fine‑tuning stage for flow matching models to align outputs with human preferences without re‑training entire long trajectories.
impact: Practitioners can efficiently align pre‑trained flow matching generators to human preferences, improving global image/layout quality and reducing fine‑tuning cost and instability compared to full trajectory backpropagation methods.

paper_title: LeapAlign: Post-Training Flow Matching Models at Any Generation Step by Building Two-Step Trajectories
paper_authors: Zhanhao Liang, Tao Yang, Jie Wu, Chengjian Feng, Liang Zheng
